back: Syntax: breaks language rules, program will not run. Logic: wrong result, no message. Run-time: stops while running.
Dry run: follow the code by hand with a trace table. Walkthrough: explain the code to colleagues who look for errors.
White-box: tests chosen from the code (every path). Black-box: tests chosen from the specification.
Alpha: developer's own staff, in-house. Beta: selected real users. Acceptance: the customer checks against the requirements.
Integration: modules tested together. Stub: a simple stand-in for a module not yet written.
Normal (valid), abnormal (invalid, including just outside the range) and extreme (valid, at the boundary).
Test number, purpose, test data, expected result (written first), actual result, pass or fail.
Corrective: fix faults. Adaptive: respond to change. Perfective: improve or add features.
After a change repeat the earlier tests to check that nothing else has stopped working.
